Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed behavior: Several worker pods fell back to CPU inference during a burst (autoscaler scheduling jitter + a recent kernel selection tweak). During fallback we saw serialization + tokenization overhead causing p95 to spike and a small number of requests to time out (manifesting as 502/504).
- Impact window: ~2026-02-12T08:27:00 -> 2026-02-12T08:49:30 EST (recovery followed autoscaler stabilization and a temporary pin to dedicated pool).
- Evidence collected: attached sample_request_traces_0212.jsonl (redacted request payloads), latency_graphs_02-12.pdf, and a short CSV of request_ids that errored.

Immediate mitigation suggestions taken:
1) Pin FinCo traffic to Dedicated pool (done, 08:50).
2) Roll back kernel scheduling change (rollback in progress).
3) Increase min replicas for burst windows.

For the preservation package: we need the full server-side traces (inference-engine logs, proxy/nginx logs, autoscaler events) for 2026-02-12T08:00:00 -> 2026-02-12T10:00:00. I uploaded a pointer to the collection folder here: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/finco-20260212-preservation and attached a SAMPLE file to this thread.

Notes on PII/tokens: the sample traces have been redacted to remove payload content; we can provide metadata-only traces (request_id, latency, status, model, node_id) in the preservation bundle. If FinCo requires full request bodies for forensic reasons, we need an approval path; discuss encrypting/exporting under an HSM-wrapped bundle and include chain-of-custody.

—Rishi

Thanks — preserving chain-of-custody steps here. Proposed actions (security owner: Marcus Lin):
1) Snapshot and lock logs for 2026-02-12T08:00 -> 2026-02-12T10:00. Disable rotation for the impacted buckets.
2) Export KMS/HSM audit events for any key usage related to payload encryption in that window.

Daniel —

Thanks again for flagging this. Apologies for the disruption — we've completed an initial investigation and preservation step and wanted to summarize next actions and timelines.

What happened (summary): an autoscaler scheduling regression combined with a kernel selection change caused a short window where several worker nodes fell back to CPU, increasing per-request latency and producing a small number of timeouts (08:27–08:49 EST). Rishi has rolled back the kernel change and we've pinned FinCo traffic to a dedicated pool to avoid recurrence during bursts.

Evidence & preservation steps we've taken:
- Locked and snapshot the server-side logs for 2026-02-12T08:00:00 -> 2026-02-12T10:00:00.
- Exported metadata traces (request_id, latency, status, model, node_id). Attached a manifest describing the preservation package.
- We will produce a signed evidence bundle (tar.gz + SHA256 + security manifest) by EOD 2026-02-15 and provide a time-limited download link.
- KMS/HSM audit events covering that window will be included; no manual key unwraps were performed.

To confirm: please let us know whether you require full request payloads for the forensic review. If so, we will prepare an export under an HSM-wrapped package and will require a signed export authorization from FinCo security (standard practice).

Attachments: incident_preservation_manifest.txt (high-level list of files we will include), latency_graphs_02-12.pdf, sample_request_traces_0212.jsonl.

We recognize this is board-level for you — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the package.
